overview: From 2026-09-06 to 2026-09-13, ethereum-optimism/specs had 5 new PRs (2 merged), 1 new issues, and 24 active contributors.

topIssues.title: zk: Align ZK dispute game terminology with the interop dependency set
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:**

The ZK dispute game pages use two terms for the set of chains that a super root commits to. Neither term matches the one the interop pages use.

The interop pages call this the [dependency set](https://specs.optimism.io/interop/dependency-set.html). The ZK pages call it the "chain set" and the "interop set", sometimes in the same sentence.

`specs/fault-proof/stage-one/zk/zk-dispute-game.md` defines "Chain Set" as its own term:

```
### Chain Set

The set of chains whose output roots are committed to by a super root. Defined by the
`SuperRootProof` preimage in `extraData`. In a standalone deployment the chain set contains
exactly one chain.
```

Two assumptions are named after it: `aZKG-008: Super Root Preimage Faithfully Represents the Chain Set` and `aZKG-009: Chain Set Is Stable During the Prove Window`.

"Interop set" is also used where the set can hold a single chain, which reads as a contradiction:

- `specs/fault-proof/zk-fault-proof-vm.md`: "In a standalone deployment (single chain), the interop set contains exactly one chain."
- `specs/fault-proof/stage-one/zk/zk-interface.md`: "cover every chain in the interop set (or a single entry in standalone deployments)"

Affected files:

- `specs/fault-proof/zk-fault-proof-vm.md`
- `specs/fault-proof/stage-one/zk/zk-dispute-game.md`
- `specs/fault-proof/stage-one/zk/zk-interface.md`
- `specs/fault-proof/stage-one/zk/zk-migration.md`

Suggested fix: use "dependency set" everywhere, and state that the dependency set may contain a single chain. This removes the need for a separate standalone term. Renaming the two assumptions changes their headings, so the anchors change.

Context: ethereum-optimism/specs#939 removed a "Chain Set" section from the super root dispute game page for this reason, and uses "dependency set" instead.

topPRs.title: opcm: add OPContractsManagerMigrator spec
topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
## Description
Specifies `OPContractsManagerMigrator` and `OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator`, the OPCM
components that merge independent OP Stack chains into a single interop set.

topPRs.title: fault-proof: Move super root dispute game out of the interop section
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Super root dispute games ship before interop activates. A chain proposes super roots with a dependency set of one chain, and the consolidation step then has no executing message to validate. Each chain keeps its own `DisputeGameFactory` and `AnchorStateRegistry` until it joins the op-governed dependency set.

The fault proof page moves from `specs/interop/` to `specs/fault-proof/stage-one/super-fault-dispute-game.md`, with a `book.toml` redirect so the published URL still resolves. The page drops the statements that make the game interop specific and states when consolidation has nothing to validate.

The `l2-receipts` and `l2-block-data` pre-image hints stay gated on interop. Both are sent only from consolidation, which the client skips entirely when interop is inactive. The chain ID requirement on the other L2 hints now depends on the state transition the program verifies, not on the interop hardfork.

`OptimismPortal` gains a note on `migrateToSharedDisputeGame` beside the shared `ETHLockbox` migration. This also corrects two references to `migrateToSuperRoots`, which no longer exists.

Open as a draft for terminology review.

topPRs.title: docs(superchain-upgrades): disallow simultaneous upgrade activations
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
Adds a general activation rule: two network upgrades MUST NOT activate at the same L2 block timestamp, unless that timestamp is at or before genesis (where upgrades activate in the genesis block itself and conventionally share timestamp `0`).

The restriction was already real but undocumented — nothing in the specs constrained activation-time ordering, and [`checkFork`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-node/rollup/types.go#L465-L480) in op-node explicitly permits equality. [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22828](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22828) is what surfaced it: Karst and Lagoon activating at the same non-genesis timestamp both add upgrade gas, but the reconstruction helpers only subtract Karst's allocation, so the inflated gas limit persists.

Per the thread discussion, the rule is stated once under "Activation rules" rather than repeated in each fork's own specification. Rationale captured in the text: each upgrade's activation-block behavior is only defined against a chain where every prior upgrade is active and every later one is not, so supporting overlapping activations would mean specifying and testing every combination of upgrades that could activate together.

The wording is scoped to OP-Stack network upgrades — it deliberately does not constrain an OP-Stack upgrade timestamp against an L1 fork timestamp on the same chain (e.g. Upgrade 15 sets `pragueTime == isthmusTime`).

The second commit adds a non-retroactivity note, because six chains in the superchain registry already violate the rule: Celo mainnet activated Holocene and Isthmus at `1752073200` (genesis `1742957258`), and sepolia/boba, sepolia/lisk, sepolia/mode, sepolia/race and sepolia/soneium-minato each share a post-genesis timestamp between two earlier upgrades. Their activation history cannot be changed, so the rule has to bind newly scheduled activations rather than all historical configs.

Companion monorepo PR — docs plus the strengthened rollup-config validation: [ethereum-optimism/optimism#22838](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22838)

Prompted by: @sebastianst

topPRs.title: specs: remove Alt-DA specification
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
Removes the experimental Alt-DA specification and retires batcher transaction version 1. Old Plasma and Alt-DA URLs redirect to the supported Ethereum DA transaction format.

Companion to ethereum-optimism/optimism#22668 and ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1318.

completedItems.title: deposits: Clarify init code size limit
completedItems.body: Clarifies deposit transaction execution for contract creation. Deposit transactions do not check init code size, so L1 constraints bound the maximum size.
